en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for gastric hyperacidity, heartburn, stomach discomfort, abdominal bloating, food stagnation, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching, indigestion, loss of appetite (poor appetite), overeating, promotion of digestion, and abdominal bloating caused by indigestion.
en.usage:

Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption; children (under 15 years); pregnant women or women who may be pregnant; or breastfeeding women.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have experienced an allergic reaction, have kidney impairment or liver impairment, are hypersensitive to Yellow No. 4 or have experienced an allergic reaction to it, have high blood pressure or are elderly, or have a heart or kidney disorder or edema. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

Do not take together with gastrointestinal analgesics or antispasmodics. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with potassium-containing preparations, licorice-containing preparations, preparations containing glycyrrhizic acid or its salts, loop diuretics (furosemide, ethacrynic acid), or thiazide diuretics (trichlormethiazide).

Stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist if any of the following occur: allergic symptoms (rash, itching, etc.); rarely palpitations, drowsiness, dizziness, fatigue, headache, constipation, or dry mouth; rapid heartbeat; elevated GOT and GPT; decreased urine volume; swelling of the face, hands, or feet; heavy eyelids; stiff hands; rising blood pressure; headache; weakness; limb cramps; or paralysis.

en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for supply of vitamins B1, B2, B6, C, and E during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, and old age; for relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (low back pain, stiff shoulders, etc.), beriberi, eye fatigue, and pigmentation (freckles and dark spots) caused by sunlight or skin conditions; for prevention of gum bleeding and nosebleeds; and for supply of zinc.
en.usage:
Children aged 12 or older and adults take 2 tablets once a day, or 1 tablet 2 times a day.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Warning: an overdose in children aged 6 or under can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: patients hypersensitive to this medicine; hemochromatosis (a disease in which iron deposits in the liver and pancreas due to abnormal iron metabolism); hemosiderosis; non-iron-deficiency anemia; or patients with hereditary problems such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which excessive oxalate is excreted in the urine), a thrombotic (blood vessel blockage) predisposition, or folic acid deficiency; if you are a pregnant woman or a woman who may be pregnant, a breastfeeding woman, or a premature or young infant; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction, kidney disorder, hypoproteinemia, gout, or kidney stones; folic acid deficiency; or hypersensitivity or a history of allergic reaction to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep strictly to the stated dosage and directions.

When giving this medicine to children, administer it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of blood glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values.

Do not use together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist when using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

Stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist if any of the following occur: stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, stomatitis (mouth inflammation), loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, hives, itching, photosensitivity reactions, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, fever, coma, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, gastrointestinal disorders, digestive disorders, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, menstruation starting earlier than expected or gradually becoming heavier, or prolonged bleeding.
